name: Neurology
boundaries: Neurology: fundamental discoveries and enabling technologies within this field. Include cross-field consequences where the central advance belongs to this field; exclude routine incremental optimization. Use the historical breakthroughs in the prompt to calibrate revolutionary impact.

original_dispositions.reason: NRL-11 addresses established Alzheimer’s; prevention is also covered by NRL-09. Other tauopathies would require their own evidence. The proposed single trigger and one-time cure are not assumed.
Biological reconnection is distinct from the electronic bridge in NRL-17.

original_dispositions.original_title: Multiple sclerosis immune reset and remyelination
original_dispositions.reason: The outcome is retained without assuming that complete immune reset or full axonal repair is already feasible.

Covered in part by NRL-07 and added as NRL-17. Communication and movement/sensation are separately testable. Millions of neurons, zero response, memory restoration and human–AI symbiosis are not treated as demonstrated or necessary consequences.
Mechanism, prevention and recovery of established impairment are distinguished.
Near-zero infarct is retained as an aspiration rather than a claim that every stroke can be rescued.
Lasting seizure freedom is distinguished from continued device-dependent suppression.

original_dispositions.original_title: Vision after optic-nerve or cortical damage
original_dispositions.reason: Covered in part by NRL-08 and added as NRL-16. A prosthesis requires suitable surviving visual circuits; biological repair of the optic nerve or visual cortex needs separate evidence.

original_dispositions.original_title: Unified mechanism and cure for autism
original_dispositions.reason: A universal defect and “normalization” of autistic traits are not established or necessary endpoints. Autism is heterogeneous, and the historical formulation does not specify a sufficiently grounded, patient-defined capability beyond an important unsolved problem. The evidence of genetic diversity does not rule out useful shared mechanisms.
The testable concept is a causally established and treatable shared mechanism; one universal regulator and reversal of lost neurons remain unproven.
